- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) after a spike, model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or adjust downward sharply.  
- After a sharp upward spike in price, model frequently overcorrects downward; apply a “mean reversion buffer” — don’t drop below 10% below prior peak unless sentiment confirms trend reversal.  
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, flag for “overshoot correction” — reduce by 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67 → 1.00 → 0.33), model may misread momentum; use sentiment-weighted moving average to smooth forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows early drop after spike, model often fails to anticipate; adjust downward by 2–5% in first 3–5 days if sentiment turns negative.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and price is trending, model often underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast if no event context suggests otherwise.  
- If model forecast is >10% above true outcome for 3 consecutive days, apply “lag correction” — reduce by 0.5–1% per day until sentiment or price confirms continuation.
